newsitem.title: UK: LME base metals keep crumbling, end PM kerb lower.
newsitem.headline: LME base metals keep crumbling, end PM kerb lower.

text.p: Base metals eased their grip on recent gains on Wednesday as prices eroded in lacklustre trade.
Three months copper drifted lower throughout the day and finished the kerb at the day's lows of $2,375, down $20 from the previous close.
It had started strong above $2,400, thanks in part to news that Asarco's copper output in southern Peru had been curtailed due to flooding.
But traders said the news was quickly priced into the market and had found no follow-through buying. Cash/threes backwardation narrowed to $52/$62, from around $70 earlier this week.
"The metals have all been drifting lower, having run into profit taking rather than aggressive selling," said analyst William Adams of Rudolf Wolff.
"And also the buyers have stepped aside. Customers are a bit nervous after prices have consistantly hit new highs every day with no fundamental news," he added.
Aluminium similarly crumbled below important nearby support at $1,680 and settled at $1,673, a decline of $13.
Dampening sentiment was news that Russian producers revised up the country's primary aluminium exports for 1996 to 2.44 million tonnes, from 2.37 million tonnes previously.
The Kontsern Alyuminiy producers group said 1997 exports would be about the same as last year, and 1997 primary aluminium output was forecast to rise by two to three percent on 1996.
Zinc settled $10 lower to $1,240, the level which earlier this week had heralded the metal's rise to 4-1/2 year highs.
Wednesday's March options declaration had little noticable effect on the base metals, with futures prices settling between key strikes in most cases.
Lead, however, sank sharply as market makers unwound their hedges for the key $625 call options, traders noted.
Chinese selling was also said to be strongly pressuring the market.

Abundant lending in the market had also relieved most of the tightness in April dates which had sent cash/threes flaring into a $20 backwardation earlier this week. They were last at a $5/$6 backwardation.
Prices posted a decline of $18, settling at $680. Analysts said the $675/$680 area was important support which if breached would target $665, analysts said.
Nickel traded in a relatively narrow range following Tuesday's sharp losses and ended the kerb just $20 easier at $8,080.
Tin was also little changed at $5,835, down $25, while alloy was last quoted at $1,553/55, compared to $1,555 on Tuesday.
